paraphrase: Subhūti says he does not find, apprehend or see any dharma called 'bodhisattva', nor any called 'perfection of wisdom'; if, hearing this, a bodhisattva's mind is not cowed or frightened, that bodhisattva is to be instructed in the perfection of wisdom — this very non-apprehension is his coursing in it.

paraphrase: The bodhisattva coursing in the perfection of wisdom should train so as not even to conceive of (manyeta) the thought of awakening, because that thought is no-thought: the essential nature of thought is luminous.

paraphrase: The bodhisattva is 'great being' (mahāsattva) because he is armed with the great armor: he thinks 'I must lead countless beings to nirvāṇa', and yet there are none who lead or are led; he leads them all to nirvāṇa and no being at all has been led to nirvāṇa, because that is the true nature of dharmas — like a magician who conjures a great crowd and makes it vanish.

paraphrase: The bodhisattva does not take hold of form or the other aggregates and does not even think of nirvāṇa; yet he does not enter nirvāṇa midway, before completing the ten powers of a Tathāgata and the other buddha-qualities.

paraphrase: Hearing that consciousness is like an illusion, bodhisattvas new to the vehicle may be frightened; they tremble if they are in the hands of bad friends; the good friends of the great-armored bodhisattva are those who teach the perfections and expose Māra's deeds.

paraphrase: Subhūti tells the gods that beings are like an illusion, like a dream; all dharmas, the fruits of the path, perfect buddhahood and even nirvāṇa are like an illusion and a dream — and if there were any dharma more distinguished than nirvāṇa, that too would be like an illusion and a dream.

paraphrase: Rejoicing (anumodanā) in all merit and dedicating (pariṇāmanā) it to awakening is supreme when done without apprehending the merit, the dedicator or awakening as things; dedication made while seizing on marks is like good food mixed with poison — 'poisoned and with a thorn'.

paraphrase: The purity of form is the purity of the fruit, and the purity of the fruit is the purity of form; the two are not two, not divided, not cut apart — likewise for the other aggregates and all-knowledge; this purity is 'deep'.

paraphrase: Māra's deeds (mārakarma) that obstruct the perfection of wisdom: eloquence that comes slowly or is scattered; copying it while yawning, laughing or distracted; losing interest; turning from it to seek sūtras that lead to the śrāvaka and pratyekabuddha levels — like a builder who wants to build a palace the size of Vaijayanta but measures it by the orbit of the sun and moon.

paraphrase: As sons protect and cherish the mother who bore them, so the Tathāgatas cherish the perfection of wisdom: she is their mother, their genetrix, who shows them the world; understanding suchness they know the world's suchness, non-falseness and unaltered suchness, and thus are called Tathāgata.

paraphrase: A bodhisattva with faith and zeal but without the perfection of wisdom and skillful means will fall short, like a man crossing water with an unbaked pot or a merchant launching an unrepaired ship laden with goods: both are lost; with wisdom and skillful means he is like a baked pot or a well-fitted ship that reaches its destination.

paraphrase: The suchness of the Tathāgata and the suchness of all dharmas are one suchness, undivided, unaltered; Subhūti is 'born after' (anujāta) the Tathāgata because he follows this suchness; the suchness is not past, future or present.
notes: Reference from the unit author's knowledge at chapter level; passage not read in a local text in this phase.

paraphrase: A bodhisattva without the perfection of wisdom and skillful means is like a huge bird without wings that jumps from the heaven of the Thirty-Three to reach Jambudvīpa: it cannot turn back and is broken on the ground — he falls to the level of the śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas.

paraphrase: Signs, marks and tokens of the irreversible (avinivartanīya) bodhisattva: he does not look to other teachers or doubt; he establishes others in the ten wholesome ways and does not break them even in dreams; he is not moved when Māra, even in the Buddha's form, tells him the teaching is not the Buddha's word.
notes: Passage located and read in the local e-text (see location.section); paraphrase by U39 (skeleton phase, fidelity not yet checked).

paraphrase: Does karma done in a dream accumulate? As all dharmas are like dreams, a dream-deed does not accumulate in itself; but when one wakes and dwells on it with discrimination (e.g. 'I killed'), it does accumulate. The bodhisattva may cultivate the three doors of liberation even in dreams. The goddess of the Ganges receives the prediction that she will become the buddha Suvarṇapuṣpa.
notes: Passage located and read in the local e-text (see location.section); paraphrase by U39 (skeleton phase, fidelity not yet checked).

paraphrase: Endowed with skillful means and upheld by the perfection of wisdom, the bodhisattva dwells in emptiness and the signless yet does not realize the reality-limit (bhūtakoṭi) until his roots of merit are ripe for full awakening — like a bird that moves through space without falling and without resting anywhere, or an archer who keeps arrows in the air by shooting each into the last; his resolve not to abandon beings is his protection.

paraphrase: The good friends (kalyāṇamitra) of the bodhisattva are the buddhas and the six perfections; the perfection of wisdom goes before the other five as their leader, guide, mother and nurse — without it the other five do not even receive the name 'perfection'.

paraphrase: A bodhisattva who, predicted or not, quarrels with, despises or is angry at other bodhisattvas must remain in saṃsāra as many aeons as the moments of that anger; he should resolve never to be angry even at those who wrong him and to confess such thoughts.

paraphrase: The bodhisattva coursing in the perfection of wisdom does not discriminate that awakening is near or the śrāvaka level far, as a man conjured by a magician does not think 'the magician is near, the crowd far', because the perfection of wisdom is free of discrimination.

paraphrase: Sadāprarudita, told by a voice in the forest to go east without regard for body, life or gain, seeks the perfection of wisdom; to honor the teacher Dharmodgata he tries to sell his own body in the market, and when Māra blocks buyers he cuts his flesh and blood for Śakra, who is testing him; his resolve is rewarded.

paraphrase: Dharmodgata teaches that the Tathāgatas neither come from anywhere nor go anywhere, for non-arising, the reality-limit, emptiness and suchness neither come nor go, and the Tathāgata is these; like the water of a mirage that a thirsty man runs after, which came from no ocean and goes to none.

paraphrase: The Buddha entrusts the perfection of wisdom to Ānanda: it brings forth the knowledge of the all-knowing; it is to be heard, learned, kept, recited, mastered, copied and honored; while it is honored the Buddha is present.

paraphrase: A bodhisattva who wishes to train in the emptinesses should train in the perfection of wisdom: the emptiness of the internal, of the external, of both, of emptiness, the great emptiness, of the ultimate, of the conditioned, of the unconditioned, the absolute emptiness, of the beginningless, of non-rejection, of essential nature, of all dharmas, of own-marks, of the non-apprehended, of the own-being of non-being, of being, of non-being, of own-being and of other-being (twenty).

paraphrase: The sameness of bodhisattvas is the emptinesses: form is empty of form, feeling of feeling, and so for the aggregates, elements, sense-fields, links of dependent origination, the perfections, the wings of awakening, the truths, the powers and the buddha-qualities — each empty of itself.

paraphrase: Subhūti asks how one who has set out in the bodhisattva-vehicle should stand, proceed and control the mind.

paraphrase: The bodhisattva should resolve: 'however many beings there are — egg-born, womb-born, moisture-born, spontaneously born, with form or without, with perception or without — all must be led by me to nirvāṇa without remainder'; yet though countless beings are so led, no being at all is led to nirvāṇa, for if the notion of a being, a self, a soul or a person occurs in a bodhisattva, he is not to be called a bodhisattva.

So as not to reveal (yathā na prakāśayet). As stars, a fault of vision, a lamp, a mock show, dew, a bubble, a dream, lightning and a cloud — so should one see the conditioned.
